name: Rh isoimmunisation
fullName: Rh isoimmunisation: anti-D prophylaxis, fetal surveillance and haemolytic disease of the newborn
subtitle: Anti-D and haemolytic disease of the newborn
oneLine: Maternal RhD alloimmunisation, anti-D prophylaxis schedules, middle cerebral artery Doppler surveillance, and intrauterine blood transfusion

skill.particulars.demographics.expect: In suspected Rh isoimmunisation, maternal blood group and Rh typing must be verified from laboratory reports, not memory. Paternal blood group and Rh typing are equally essential: if the biological father is confirmed Rh-negative, the fetus is obligatorily Rh-negative and isoimmunisation cannot occur.

skill.hx.chief_complaints.expect: Expect an asymptomatic woman presenting after routine antenatal blood grouping revealed an Rh-negative blood group or a positive indirect Coombs test. An alloimmunised fetus remains completely silent until profound anaemia or hydrops causes reduced movements or maternal mirror syndrome.

skill.hx.obg.booking_lmp.expect: Establish reliable gestational age from last menstrual period and first-trimester dating ultrasound. Precise dating is mandatory because middle cerebral artery Doppler peak systolic velocity thresholds change weekly.

chapters.title: Past, personal, drug and family history

skill.hx.obg.medical_family_drug.expect: Inquire specifically into prior blood transfusions, organ transplantation, or parenteral exposure that could sensitise to Rh or atypical red cell antigens, as well as family history of haemolytic disease.

skill.hx.obg.previous_pregnancies.expect: Meticulously record each previous gestation: full-term deliveries, abortions, ectopic pregnancies, invasive procedures, and whether the babies developed neonatal jaundice or received phototherapy. Verify whether anti-D was administered after each event.

skill.gen.appearance.expect: The mother is usually in good general condition and comfortable. Look for generalized maternal oedema, facial puffiness, or pallor, which in advanced hydrops may signal maternal mirror syndrome.

skill.gen.vitals.expect: Vitals are typically normal. Blood pressure elevation with rapid weight gain and generalized fluid overload in the presence of fetal hydrops suggests maternal mirror syndrome.

skill.gen.edema.expect: Pedal and facial oedema are usually absent in uncomplicated alloimmunisation. The development of sudden, severe generalized oedema points towards Ballantyne mirror syndrome.

skill.gen.cyanosis.expect: Cyanosis is absent in uncomplicated pregnancy. Central cyanosis with breathlessness warrants urgent evaluation for maternal pulmonary oedema in mirror syndrome.

skill.exam.obg.preg_prep_inspect.expect: Inspect abdominal contour for symmetrical distension. Excessive abdominal distension with tense, shiny skin suggests polyhydramnios associated with fetal hydrops.

skill.exam.obg.fundal_height.expect: Fundal height corresponds to gestational age in early or mild disease, but may exceed dates by 3 cm or more if hydropic placentomegaly and polyhydramnios have developed.

skill.exam.obg.leopold.expect: Palpation typically reveals normal lie and presentation. In the presence of polyhydramnios, fetal parts feel fluid-cushioned and difficult to outline, with an easily ballotable fetus.

skill.exam.obg.fetal_heart.expect: Fetal heart sounds are regular with a normal baseline of 110 to 160 bpm. Severe fetal anaemia produces persistent fetal tachycardia or an ominous sinusoidal rhythm.

skill.rh.basics.title: What Rh isoimmunisation and alloimmunisation are
skill.rh.basics.oneLine: Erythrocyte antigen incompatibility, transplacental sensitisation, maternal IgG transfer, and fetal extravascular haemolysis
skill.rh.basics.why: Rh isoimmunisation is the classic immunohaematological model of maternal-fetal conflict. Understanding how fetomaternal haemorrhage elicits anti-D antibodies that cross the placenta to destroy fetal erythrocytes provides the pathophysiological rationale for routine prophylaxis, antibody titration, Doppler surveillance, and timely intrauterine transfusion.

teach.heading: The Rh blood group system and antigen D
teach.body:
The Rh blood group system comprises multiple surface protein antigens encoded on chromosome 1, of which antigen D is by far the most potent immunogen. Individuals possessing the D antigen on their red blood cells are classified as Rh-positive, while those lacking it are Rh-negative.

In India, approximately 5 to 6 percent of pregnant women are Rh-negative, compared with about 15 percent in Caucasian populations.

teach.heading: Primary sensitisation versus secondary immune response
Pathogenesis of fetal anaemia and hydrops fetalis
teach.body:
When maternal IgG anti-D antibodies enter the fetal circulation, they coat Rh-positive fetal red cells. Macrophages in the fetal spleen recognise the Fc portion and phagocytose the erythrocytes, producing progressive extravascular haemolysis.

Severe fetal anaemia stimulates extramedullary haematopoiesis in the liver and spleen. Hepatosplenomegaly leads to portal hypertension, hypoalbuminaemia, high-output cardiac failure, and hydrops fetalis.

probes.q: Which specific immunoglobulin isotype crosses the placenta to cause fetal red cell destruction in Rh isoimmunisation, and why does IgM not cross?
probes.a: IgG crosses the placenta actively via neonatal Fc receptors on the syncytiotrophoblast, whereas IgM is a large pentameric molecule that cannot cross the placental barrier.

probes.q: What is the sequence of pathophysiological changes linking severe fetal anaemia to the development of hydrops fetalis?
probes.a: Severe anaemia triggers hepatic extramedullary haematopoiesis, causing portal hypertension, hepatic parenchymal disruption, hypoalbuminaemia, capillary leakage, and high-output cardiac failure with generalised oedema.

sources.locator: Alloimmunization: pathophysiology of Rh disease and fetal hydrops

skill.rh.findings.title: Clinical and ultrasound manifestations of fetal anaemia and hydrops fetalis
skill.rh.findings.oneLine: Recognising fetal hyperdynamic circulation, sinusoidal CTG, ultrasound markers of effusions, and maternal mirror syndrome
skill.rh.findings.why: Rh isoimmunisation is clinically occult in the mother until late stages, while the fetus deteriorates from severe anaemia to irreversible hydropic decompensation. Mastering the spectrum from subtle Doppler velocity elevations and sinusoidal heart traces to frank fluid accumulation ensures timely intervention before intrauterine death.

teach.heading: The clinical presentation of fetal anaemia
teach.body:
An Rh-sensitised pregnancy is typically free of maternal symptoms until severe fetal compromise develops. Maternal perception of reduced fetal movements is an alarming sign indicating critical tissue hypoxia.

On physical examination, fundal height may exceed dates due to polyhydramnios and placentomegaly. Fetal heart auscultation may reveal resting fetal tachycardia, while cardiotocography demonstrates an ominous sinusoidal baseline pattern.

teach.heading: Ultrasound features of hydrops fetalis
Maternal mirror syndrome (Ballantyne syndrome)
teach.body:
In advanced hydrops fetalis, the mother may develop generalized oedema, sudden weight gain, hypertension, and proteinuria that mirrors the hydropic fetus. This life-threatening state represents maternal endotheliopathy provoked by placental hyperplacentosis.

Maternal mirror syndrome can lead to acute pulmonary oedema and mandates urgent delivery or fetal therapy, following which maternal features resolve rapidly.

probes.q: What cardiotocography pattern is classically associated with severe, life-threatening fetal anaemia in Rh alloimmunisation?
probes.a: A sinusoidal fetal heart rate pattern, characterized by a smooth, undulating, sine-wave oscillation with a frequency of 2 to 5 cycles per minute, indicates severe fetal anaemia and impending acidemia.

probes.q: What ultrasound criteria establish the formal diagnosis of hydrops fetalis?
probes.a: Hydrops fetalis is diagnosed on ultrasound by pathological fluid accumulation in at least two fetal body cavities, such as ascites, pleural effusion, or pericardial effusion, often accompanied by subcutaneous skin oedema.

sources.locator: Hydrops fetalis: sonographic diagnosis and clinical features

skill.rh.summary.title: The clinical summary in Rh negative pregnancy
skill.rh.summary.oneLine: Synthesising maternal Rh status, antibody titres, previous obstetric history, and fetal Doppler metrics
skill.rh.summary.why: The clinical summary transforms scattered laboratory titres, past obstetric losses, and ultrasound Doppler numbers into a coherent case synthesis. Presenting a crisp, prioritized summary enables the multidisciplinary team to determine whether the patient needs simple antibody re-titration, middle cerebral artery surveillance, or immediate intrauterine transfusion.

teach.heading: The four pillars of the Rh summary
teach.body:
A clinical summary in Rh isoimmunisation must integrate four distinct components: maternal antibody status, partner status, obstetric history of sensitising events, and current fetal well-being.

Stating maternal blood group alone is insufficient; the clinician must immediately qualify whether the woman is unsensitised or sensitised, the current antibody titre, and whether the critical threshold has been reached.

teach.heading: Structuring the synthesis for decision-making

rows: Exceeds critical titre; triggers MCA Doppler
Prior unprophylaxed term birth and miscarriage
MCA-PSV 1.6 MoM at 28 weeks, no hydrops

teach.heading: Synthesising for transfer and multidisciplinary care
teach.body:
When a sensitised mother reaches a critical titre or demonstrates elevated MCA Doppler velocities, the case summary serves as the transfer document to a tertiary fetal medicine unit.

The summary must highlight gestational age, fetal viability, latest MCA-PSV in multiples of the median, presence of hydrops, and blood bank coordination for specialised donor blood.

probes.q: What crucial distinction separates an unsensitised Rh-negative pregnancy summary from a sensitised pregnancy summary?
probes.a: An unsensitised pregnancy summary focuses on anti-D prophylaxis schedules and screening intervals, whereas a sensitised summary focuses on antibody titres, critical thresholds, and fetal anaemia surveillance.

probes.q: Why is establishing paternal RhD zygosity important when evaluating an Rh-alloimmunised pregnant woman?
probes.a: If the father is homozygous for RhD, all offspring will be Rh-positive and at risk; if he is heterozygous, there is a 50 percent chance the fetus is Rh-negative and completely unaffected.

skill.rh.differential.title: Differential diagnosis of fetal anaemia and hydrops fetalis
skill.rh.differential.oneLine: Differentiating RhD disease from ABO incompatibility, minor red cell antibodies, viral infections, and non-immune hydrops
skill.rh.differential.why: Not all fetal anaemia or hydrops is caused by RhD isoimmunisation. More than 85 percent of hydrops cases today are non-immune. Differentiating RhD alloimmunisation from ABO incompatibility, atypical red cell antibodies, congenital infections such as parvovirus B19, and alpha thalassaemia major directs appropriate laboratory testing and avoids administering useless anti-D.

teach.heading: Immune versus non-immune hydrops fetalis
teach.body:
Fetal hydrops is divided into immune hydrops (alloimmune haemolytic disease) and non-immune hydrops fetalis (NIHF). With widespread anti-D prophylaxis, non-immune causes now account for nearly 90 percent of cases.

Non-immune hydrops encompasses cardiovascular malformations, chromosomal anomalies (such as Turner syndrome and trisomy 21), congenital infections, twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome, and inborn errors of metabolism.

teach.heading: Distinguishing common causes of fetal haemolysis and hydrops

rows: Severe fetal anaemia, hydrops, IUT responsive
Mother group O, fetus group A or B
Mild neonatal jaundice, hydrops in utero is rare
Erythroid suppression in marrow, severe anaemia
Pure red cell aplasia, transient hydrops, IgM+

teach.heading: Alpha thalassaemia major and fetomaternal haemorrhage
teach.body:
In populations with high alpha thalassaemia prevalence, homozygous deletion of all four alpha globin genes produces Haemoglobin Barts hydrops fetalis, presenting with severe anaemia, hepatosplenomegaly, and massive placentomegaly in an antibody-negative mother.

Acute or chronic fetomaternal haemorrhage causes profound fetal anaemia and sinusoidal CTG without immune destruction, confirmed by a strongly positive maternal Kleihauer-Betke test.

probes.q: Why does ABO incompatibility rarely cause severe fetal anaemia or hydrops in utero compared with Rh isoimmunisation?
probes.a: ABO antigens are weakly expressed on fetal red cells and widely expressed on other fetal tissues and placenta, neutralizing maternal anti-A and anti-B antibodies before they can produce heavy fetal haemolysis.

probes.q: How does the mechanism of fetal anaemia in anti-Kell alloimmunisation differ fundamentally from RhD alloimmunisation?
probes.a: Anti-Kell antibodies destroy early erythroid progenitor cells in fetal bone marrow causing hyporegenerative anaemia, unlike RhD antibodies which cause predominantly peripheral extravascular splenic haemolysis.

sources.locator: Alloimmunization: differential diagnosis and non-immune hydrops

skill.ix.rh.workup.title: Antibody titration, cell-free fetal DNA, MCA Doppler PSV and fetal blood sampling
skill.ix.rh.workup.oneLine: Diagnostic algorithm from indirect Coombs test and non-invasive prenatal testing to serial MCA Doppler and cordocentesis
skill.ix.rh.workup.why: Modern management of Rh isoimmunisation has evolved from invasive amniocentesis to non-invasive ultrasound and molecular testing. Selecting maternal antibody titration, maternal plasma cell-free fetal DNA for RhD genotyping, and serial middle cerebral artery Doppler allows precise timing of invasive fetal blood sampling and blood transfusion while eliminating procedural fetal loss.

teach.heading: Maternal antibody titration and critical titres
teach.body:
All pregnant women undergo ABO and Rh typing with an indirect Coombs test (ICT) or indirect antiglobulin test (IAT) at booking.

In an unsensitised Rh-negative woman, the antibody screen is repeated at 28 weeks. In an alloimmunised woman, the antibody is identified and titrated. When the titre reaches the critical threshold (typically 1:16 to 1:32), titration ceases to correlate with severity, and direct fetal monitoring begins.

teach.heading: Cell-free fetal DNA and non-invasive prenatal testing
teach.body:
Maternal plasma cell-free fetal DNA (cffDNA) testing detects fetal RHD gene fragments from 10 to 12 weeks of gestation with diagnostic accuracy exceeding 99 percent.

If cffDNA confirms the fetus is RhD-negative, further intensive surveillance is unnecessary because the fetus lacks the target antigen and cannot develop haemolytic disease.

teach.heading: Middle cerebral artery Doppler and cordocentesis

rows: PSV > 1.5 MoM indicates moderate to severe anaemia
Detection of ascites, pericardial effusion, oedema
Calculates required anti-D dose after sensitising events

probes.q: What is the physiological mechanism explaining why the middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity increases as fetal anaemia worsens?
probes.a: Anaemia reduces fetal blood viscosity and triggers hyperdynamic circulation with elevated cardiac output, while selective cerebral vasodilation increases blood flow velocity in the middle cerebral artery.

probes.q: When is percutaneous umbilical blood sampling indicated in an Rh-sensitised pregnancy, and what is its main complication risk?
probes.a: Cordocentesis is indicated when MCA Doppler PSV exceeds 1.5 MoM to measure fetal haematocrit immediately prior to intrauterine transfusion; its primary risk is 1 to 2 percent procedure-related fetal loss.

skill.annex.rh.thresholds.title: Critical antibody titres, MCA Doppler PSV thresholds, and Kleihauer-Betke calculation
skill.annex.rh.thresholds.oneLine: Reference tables and mathematical formulas for indirect Coombs titres, MCA-PSV multiples of the median, and anti-D dosing
skill.annex.rh.thresholds.why: Precise numerical thresholds govern every key decision in Rh isoimmunisation: initiating Doppler scans, diagnosing moderate-to-severe fetal anaemia, timing intrauterine transfusions, and calculating the exact dose of anti-D required to clear large fetomaternal haemorrhages.

teach.heading: Critical maternal antibody titres and monitoring intervals

rows: Repeat maternal ICT every 2 to 4 weeks until 28 weeks, then fortnightly
Commence serial fetal MCA Doppler PSV scans every 1 to 2 weeks
Initiate MCA Doppler early (from 16 to 18 weeks) regardless of titre
Urgent referral to Maternal-Fetal Medicine unit

teach.heading: Mari MCA Doppler peak systolic velocity reference values

rows: Values > 1.5 MoM indicate moderate to severe anaemia
Serial scans performed every 1 to 2 weeks

teach.heading: Kleihauer-Betke test calculation for fetomaternal haemorrhage
teach.body:
The Kleihauer-Betke (acid elution) test counts fetal cells in 2,000 adult cells. Maternal blood volume is estimated as 5,000 mL, and the fetal red cell volume is calculated as: Fetal cells (%) x 50.

Because 300 micrograms (1500 IU) of anti-D neutralises up to 30 mL of fetal whole blood (15 mL of fetal packed red cells), divide the calculated volume of fetomaternal haemorrhage by 30 to determine the total 300 mcg ampoules required.

probes.q: What volume of fetal whole blood and fetal packed red cells is effectively neutralized by a standard 300 microgram dose of anti-D immunoglobulin?
probes.a: A standard dose of 300 micrograms (1500 IU) of anti-D immunoglobulin neutralizes up to 30 mL of fetal whole blood or 15 mL of fetal packed red blood cells.

probes.q: Why is anti-Kell alloimmunisation monitored with fetal MCA Doppler even when maternal antibody titres are low, such as 1:2 or 1:4?
probes.a: Anti-Kell antibodies directly suppress fetal erythroid progenitor cells in bone marrow rather than causing proportionate haemolysis, so severe fetal anaemia can develop even at very low maternal antibody titres.

sources.locator: The Use of Anti-D Immunoglobulin for RhD Prophylaxis: Kleihauer Testing and Dosing

skill.rh.diagnosis.title: Diagnostic criteria, staging, and risk stratification in Rh isoimmunisation
skill.rh.diagnosis.oneLine: Categorising unsensitised risk, critical maternal alloimmunisation, mild to severe fetal anaemia, and hydrops fetalis
skill.rh.diagnosis.why: Staging Rh isoimmunisation accurately determines the clinical trajectory from low-risk preventive care to urgent maternal-fetal intensive therapy. Formulating a precise diagnostic statement specifying maternal antibody titre, paternal zygosity, fetal MCA Doppler category, and presence of hydrops directs the surveillance schedule and delivery timing.

teach.heading: Diagnostic criteria and staging classification

rows: Low immediate fetal risk; serial antibody titres
High risk of fetal anaemia; mandatory MCA Doppler
Critical emergency; requires IUT or delivery

teach.heading: Stratifying severity of fetal anaemia
teach.body:
Fetal anaemia is stratified by middle cerebral artery Doppler velocity into mild (MCA-PSV 1.29 to 1.50 MoM), moderate (1.50 to 1.55 MoM), and severe (greater than 1.55 MoM or associated with hydrops).

When MCA-PSV exceeds 1.50 MoM, the sensitivity for detecting moderate to severe anaemia (haemoglobin deficit greater than 5 standard deviations) approaches 100 percent.

teach.heading: Constructing the complete diagnostic statement
teach.body:
A complete obstetric diagnosis must be articulated comprehensively: Gravida 3 Para 1 Live 1 Abortion 1 at 28 weeks of gestation with blood group O Rh-negative, husband B Rh-positive, Rh alloimmunisation with indirect Coombs titre 1:32, complicated by moderate-to-severe fetal anaemia on MCA Doppler (1.6 MoM) without hydrops fetalis.

This explicit statement identifies parity, gestation, immunologic status, severity, and immediate therapeutic urgency.

probes.q: What findings classify an Rh-alloimmunised pregnancy as high risk requiring immediate tertiary fetal medicine referral?
probes.a: An indirect Coombs test antibody titre reaching or exceeding 1:16 to 1:32, a rapid four-fold titre rise, an MCA Doppler PSV exceeding 1.5 MoM, or ultrasound features of hydrops fetalis.

probes.q: What components must be included in a complete diagnostic formulation for an Rh-isoimmunised pregnancy?
probes.a: The diagnosis must state maternal and paternal Rh status, parity, exact gestational age, maternal antibody titre, fetal MCA Doppler category or MoM value, and the presence or absence of hydrops fetalis.

skill.tx.rh.prophylaxis.title: Anti-D immunoprophylaxis regimens: routine antenatal and sensitising events
skill.tx.rh.prophylaxis.oneLine: Indications, timing, and dosages of polyclonal anti-D immunoglobulin in India and international guidelines
skill.tx.rh.prophylaxis.why: Anti-D immunoprophylaxis is one of the greatest successes of modern preventive obstetrics, reducing maternal alloimmunisation rates from 16 percent to under 0.2 percent. Understanding the exact dosage thresholds, administration windows, and management of sensitising events is mandatory for every clinician caring for pregnant women.
skill.tx.rh.prophylaxis.dosingNote: CliniX does not prescribe. Doses are quoted from standard obstetric protocols (Williams Obstetrics, RCOG, FOGSI) and the StewardMD Clinical KB for revision and examination purposes only.

teach.heading: Routine antenatal anti-D prophylaxis (RAADP)
teach.body:
All unsensitised Rh-negative pregnant women should receive routine antenatal anti-D prophylaxis. In India, a single dose of 300 micrograms (1500 IU) is administered intramuscularly between 28 and 30 weeks of gestation.

An alternative two-dose regimen offers 100 to 120 micrograms (500 to 625 IU) at 28 weeks and again at 34 weeks. Prophylaxis is withheld only if the biological father is confirmed Rh-negative or cell-free fetal DNA confirms an Rh-negative fetus.

teach.heading: Postpartum prophylaxis and the 72-hour window
teach.body:
Following delivery, cord blood is collected to determine neonatal ABO and Rh status and direct antiglobulin test (DAT). If the neonate is Rh-positive and the mother is unsensitised, 300 micrograms (1500 IU) of anti-D is administered intramuscularly within 72 hours.

If the 72-hour window is missed, anti-D should still be administered as soon as realized, up to 28 days postpartum, because substantial protection is still achieved.

teach.heading: Dosage regimens for sensitising events in pregnancy
Contraindications and common misconceptions
teach.body:
Anti-D immunoglobulin is completely ineffective and contraindicated in an already sensitised woman (positive ICT with anti-D antibodies). It cannot reverse or treat existing antibody production.

Anti-D must also never be given to an Rh-positive woman or an infant. Mild local pain, erythema, and low-grade fever are common side effects, while severe anaphylaxis is exceedingly rare.

probes.q: What should be done if an Rh-negative mother did not receive anti-D immunoglobulin within the standard 72-hour postpartum window?
probes.a: Anti-D immunoglobulin should still be administered as soon as the omission is recognized, up to 28 days postpartum, as partial immunological protection is still conferred.

probes.q: Why is anti-D immunoglobulin contraindicated in a pregnant woman who already has a positive indirect Coombs test for anti-D antibodies?
probes.a: Anti-D immunoglobulin is ineffective once maternal B-lymphocyte clones are actively producing endogenous anti-D antibodies, and it cannot reverse established alloimmunisation.

skill.tx.rh.management.title: Management of sensitised pregnancy: intrauterine transfusion, timing of delivery, and neonatal care
skill.tx.rh.management.oneLine: Therapeutic protocols for severe fetal anaemia, cordocentesis technique, delivery thresholds, and neonatal exchange transfusion
skill.tx.rh.management.why: When maternal alloimmunisation produces severe fetal anaemia, prompt intervention with intrauterine blood transfusion can reverse hydrops and achieve fetal survival rates exceeding 90 percent. Understanding transfusion technique, delivery timing, and neonatal resuscitation prevents intrauterine demise and bilirubin encephalopathy.
skill.tx.rh.management.dosingNote: CliniX does not prescribe. Doses are quoted from standard obstetric protocols (Williams Obstetrics, RCOG, FOGSI) and the StewardMD Clinical KB for revision and examination purposes only.

teach.heading: Intrauterine blood transfusion (IUT) technique and indications
teach.body:
Intrauterine blood transfusion is indicated when fetal MCA-PSV exceeds 1.5 MoM and cordocentesis confirms fetal haematocrit below 30 percent or haemoglobin deficit greater than 4 to 5 g/dL.

Under continuous ultrasound guidance, a 20- or 22-gauge spinal needle enters the umbilical vein at the placental insertion. Blood is infused slowly to raise fetal haematocrit to a target post-transfusion level of 40 to 45 percent.

teach.heading: Donor blood specifications for intrauterine transfusion

rows: Compatible with fetus and maternal anti-D antibodies
Prevents immune destruction by maternal antibodies
Prevents transplacental viral infection in utero
Prevents graft-versus-host disease and volume overload

teach.heading: Timing and mode of delivery in sensitised pregnancy
teach.body:
In uncomplicated sensitised pregnancies with sub-critical titres, delivery is planned at 37 to 38 weeks. In fetuses requiring repeated intrauterine transfusions, the final transfusion is performed around 34 to 35 weeks, with delivery scheduled at 35 to 37 weeks.

Antenatal corticosteroids are administered before 34 weeks for fetal lung maturity. Delivery must take place in a tertiary centre equipped with advanced neonatal intensive care.

teach.heading: Neonatal management: phototherapy and exchange transfusion
teach.body:
At delivery, cord blood is sent for haematocrit, bilirubin, blood grouping, and direct antiglobulin test (DAT). Intensive phototherapy is initiated immediately to convert unconjugated bilirubin into lumirubin.

Double-volume exchange transfusion is performed if cord bilirubin exceeds 4.5 mg/dL, haemoglobin is under 11 g/dL, or serum bilirubin rises faster than 0.5 mg/dL per hour, preventing acute bilirubin encephalopathy (kernicterus).

probes.q: What specific criteria dictate the choice and preparation of donor blood for fetal intrauterine blood transfusion?
probes.a: Donor blood must be group O Rh-negative, cross-matched against maternal serum, CMV-negative, irradiated to prevent graft-versus-host disease, leukodepleted, and packed to a haematocrit of 75 to 85 percent.

probes.q: What are the indications for immediate double-volume exchange transfusion in a newborn infant with Rh haemolytic disease?
probes.a: Indications include cord blood haemoglobin under 11 g/dL, cord bilirubin exceeding 4.5 mg/dL, bilirubin rising faster than 0.5 mg/dL per hour, or total serum bilirubin reaching exchange levels despite intensive phototherapy.

diagnosis.answer: Rh isoimmunisation (alloimmunisation) at 28 weeks of gestation with critical antibody titre 1:32 and moderate-to-severe fetal anaemia on MCA Doppler.

differentialModel.answer: Rh isoimmunisation with fetal anaemia. Differentials include ABO incompatibility in pregnancy, minor red cell alloimmunisation (anti-Kell, anti-c), congenital parvovirus B19 infection, alpha thalassaemia major, and massive fetomaternal haemorrhage.

managementModel.answer: Admit to tertiary fetal medicine unit; perform comprehensive ultrasound to rule out hydrops; prepare for percutaneous umbilical cord blood sampling (cordocentesis) and intrauterine blood transfusion using O Rh-negative irradiated washed packed red cells; administer antenatal corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity; maintain serial MCA Doppler surveillance every 1 to 2 weeks post-transfusion; plan delivery at 35 to 37 weeks in a centre with tertiary NICU facilities.

teachingPoints: Maternal Rh isoimmunisation is asymptomatic in the mother but causes progressive extravascular haemolysis and anaemia in the Rh-positive fetus due to transplacental transfer of maternal IgG anti-D antibodies.

Routine antenatal anti-D prophylaxis with 300 mcg (1500 IU) at 28 weeks and within 72 hours postpartum, plus for all sensitising events, prevents primary alloimmunisation in unsensitised Rh-negative women.

Once maternal alloimmunisation occurs and the indirect Coombs titre exceeds the critical threshold (1:16 to 1:32), serial middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity Doppler (> 1.5 MoM) accurately detects moderate-to-severe fetal anaemia non-invasively.

Definitive management of severe fetal anaemia in utero before 35 weeks is intrauterine blood transfusion via cordocentesis using group O Rh-negative irradiated packed red cells, achieving fetal survival over 90 percent.
